written: 2026-11-07, after the fixes' code and before fourth-visit-selection's header probe or the fourth visit ran. The selection's local part (13 records) was counted from the walk's log and the local tables' first lines (their separators and names) while writing this, and the identifier columns of the six DIA-NN tables (Genes, Protein.Group) were counted; no quantity value of a drawn deposit was read.
about: B3's fourth visit (research/value-scale-plan.md, B3; research/benchmark/protocol-value-scale.md, amendment 4): the records the fixes of 2026-11-07 touch, visited again with the fixed tools, in their places in the log. No detector statistic, gate or verdict is computed on any drawn deposit. Not edited after the run: a difference is reported.

faults.dia_nn_protein_groups: a DIA-NN matrix whose Genes column is empty on every row was refused ('no row has an identifier in Genes'), though each row names its protein group. Its rows are now named by Protein.Group when no row has a gene; a matrix with gene names still leaves out its rows without one. 4 records: PXD064789 (test, 2,319 rows), PXD070147 (calibration, 6,236), PXD059079 (calibration, 1,590), all with Protein.Group on every row; PXD046550 (test) has a header and no row
faults.separator: the separator was chosen from the header line alone: a tab when it holds more tabs than commas. DIA-NN names its runs by their paths, and a path may hold commas, so a tab-separated matrix was split on its commas and every row was short ('fewer than the header's'). Now the line under the header decides when it keeps exactly one separator's count. The long and Proteome Discoverer readers broke a tie for tabs, the parser for commas; they now share the parser's rule. 2 records: PXD053397 (test), PXD053298 (calibration)
faults.empty_member: an archive member of 0 bytes (a folder entry or a placeholder) could be the chosen table. It is never a candidate now. 2 records: PXD056559 (test, MaxQuant), PXD046085 (calibration, DIA-NN matrix)
faults.decimal_comma: a number written with a decimal comma ('8329,325', Spectronaut and Excel with a European region setting) failed as text where a number belongs. The owner chose to refuse it in clear words, not to read it (2026-11-07). 4 records: PXD062541 (calibration, DIA-NN report), PXD047604 (test, Spectronaut long), PXD036850 (calibration, Spectronaut long), PXD043761 (calibration, Spectronaut pivot)
faults.maxquant_case: MaxQuant's quantity columns were known only as 'LFQ intensity' and 'Intensity', spelled so; MaxQuant 1.0 to 1.2 wrote 'LFQ Intensity'. The owner chose any case (2026-11-07). 1 record: PXD054457 (calibration, kept, linear), read from its 'Intensity' columns until now

selection.rule: research/notebooks/value_scale_corpus.py, fourth_visit_reasons and cmd_fourth_visit_selection: an unparseable record whose detail holds 'no row has an identifier in Genes' or a number written with a comma; a chosen member of 0 bytes; a local table (not parquet) whose separator differs between the rule before 2026-11-07 (_separator_before) and now (remote.delimiter), or a MaxQuant table with a quantity column known only in any case; and a record the walk decided on a wide table's header alone (too few columns with header_columns, or refused on the header) whose header, read again now, decides otherwise (_header_decision_now)
selection.probe: the 1,584 records decided on a wide table's header alone (1,515 too few columns with header_columns, 69 refused on the header) have their headers read again, the header alone: the separator rule and MaxQuant's names in any case change what the header reader makes of a header too
selection.written_to: valuescale/corpus/cleanup_20261107.json, by fourth-visit-selection, before the fourth visit

expected.probe: at least 90% of the 1,584 headers can be read now, and at most 10 decide otherwise now. Each that does is visited again
expected.protein_groups: PXD064789, PXD070147 and PXD059079 are read, their rows named by protein group: kept, or a later rule (too few columns or rows, unclear label). PXD046550 is refused again by name, as a table without any identifier
expected.separator: neither PXD053397 nor PXD053298 fails with 'fewer than the header's' again: kept, or a later rule
expected.empty_member: neither PXD056559 nor PXD046085 chooses a member of 0 bytes again: another member, or no candidate
expected.decimal_comma: all 4 stay unparseable, and each detail says the column holds 'a number written with a comma'
expected.maxquant_case: PXD054457 stays kept, linear, with the same row and column counts; its cells now come from its 'LFQ Intensity' columns (counted from its header: as many as its 'Intensity' columns)
expected.nothing_else: no record outside the selection changes; the log keeps the frame's order; each revisited record keeps its earlier outcomes in revisited_from, with the third visit's revisited_for inside it where it had one, and its new reasons in revisited_for
expected.corpus: S1 and S2 still meet 59 in both splits; S3 stays short and pools with S2; still no real log table
expected.report: every B3 row keeps its pass or fail, with B3_frame failing as the owner accepted. B3_audit stays the rank-based sample's, not redrawn; B3_audit_cleanup covers the tables either clean-up visit added

audit: every table this visit keeps that was not kept before is judged under b3.json's audit_rubric, by subagents, with Claude rereading every disagreement, every doubt and every tenth agreement. It joins the third visit's under audit.json's 'cleanup' key, with the verdicts beside the others. PXD054457, added by the third visit, stays among the clean-up's tables (newly_kept skips the outcomes the clean-up's own visits gave). Its packet showed no 'LFQ intensity' column; it is rebuilt (the old one moved aside, not deleted) and judged again, the new verdict replacing the third visit's, which is kept inside it. Expected: every added table judged, and at least 90% of the clean-up's agree, as B3_audit_cleanup asks. A disagreement is excluded, as before
